source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release 26.13.1-CE-ubuntu24.04-r2 was cut (2026-11-20T07:24:11Z), by scripts/rerelease-agenda.py: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit e9c277643b02, dated 2026-11-10T18:41:03Z (source.commit_epoch).
source._build_note: Node.js vendors every dependency in its own tree (deps/: V8, libuv, OpenSSL 3.5.9, ICU 78 with full data, llhttp, nghttp2, ngtcp2, brotli, zlib, simdjson, ada, npm 11.20.0, which source_prep replaces with npm 11.21.2): configure (a python3 script) and make build them from source, with no download. `make install` lays down /opt/node/bin/node, the npm and npx links, /opt/node/lib/node_modules/npm and the headers in /opt/node/include (node-gyp builds native addons against them, in a stage that has a compiler). The checks after it refuse a build whose node or npm is not the expected version, whose crypto does not hash, or whose ICU has no German month names (small-icu would print 'M11'). Measured 2026-11-08: configure succeeds on ubuntu:24.04 (gcc 13.3, python 3.12). Tests: Node's own suite (tools/test.py) is not run in the offline build: much of it needs the network, a TTY or timing; the program set (seed_plan) runs in the image instead.
source_prep: python3 -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlretrieve('https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-11.21.2.tgz', '/tmp/npm.tgz')" && echo '8ad8563b81e71b90ef405b140bccf3ba9b5e7884ab210bd49ee4e2f4bc6f61f5  /tmp/npm.tgz' | sha256sum -c - && rm -rf deps/npm && mkdir deps/npm && tar -xzf /tmp/npm.tgz --strip-components=1 -C deps/npm && rm -f /tmp/npm.tgz && grep -q '"version": "11.21.2"' deps/npm/package.json && grep -q '"version": "6.29.1"' deps/npm/node_modules/undici/package.json && grep -q '"version": "5.0.12"' deps/npm/node_modules/brace-expansion/package.json
source._source_prep_note: npm 11.21.2 replaces the npm 11.20.0 that tag v26.13.0 carries in deps/npm, the way Node.js updates npm itself (tools/dep_updaters/update-npm.sh: download the npm release tarball, rm -rf deps/npm, extract it there with --strip-components=1). Chain 867's own scan (2026-11-08) found 6 fixable highs, all in npm 11.20.0's bundled packages: undici 6.28.0 (CVE-2026-87018, CVE-2026-19534, CVE-2026-109869, CVE-2026-109383; fixed in 6.29.1) and brace-expansion 5.0.9 (CVE-2026-102278, CVE-2026-102276; fixed in 5.0.11). npm 11.21.2 (2026-11-04), the newest npm 11 release, bundles undici 6.29.1 and brace-expansion 5.0.12. npm 11 is the line Node.js 26 ships, so the newer npm 12 is not used. npm 11.21.2 declares engines node ^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0. The tarball is the registry's (sha512 integrity sha512-7HPApk+AflMUavSseL1Pm6CnYqMIHk53x+KmuhqmTDqPkjPMgxIpTPcTqsE91EKNw4gFBJV9fnXiSdGm1DXq9A==, the same bytes as the sha256 checked here). The vendor stage has python3 and no curl, so python3 downloads it. The step refuses a tree whose npm, undici or brace-expansion is not the expected version. Node's own deps/undici (compiled into node as its fetch) and deps/minimatch are not npm's copies and are unchanged.
